source.title: NVC-1B: Scaling up Neural Video Coding Models
source.authors: Chuanbo Tang; Xi-Hua Sheng; Li Li; Dong Liu; Feng Wu

record.file_problem: The supplied text is a full paper. Its front matter identifies an arXiv version submitted to IEEE Transactions on Circuits and Systems for Video Technology, whereas the catalog metadata gives a different venue.
record.tranche_reason: The paper cites scaling laws as motivation for increasing model size, but it studies neural video compression performance rather than language-model held-out cross-entropy scaling laws or their fitted predictions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports parameter-scaling and architecture comparisons for video compression, not language-model loss, power-law fits, extrapolation, or compute-optimal allocations. The video compression outcomes are recorded as related findings, not as tests of the listed versions. The cited scaling-law results are not the paper's own results.
record.test_reason: The paper cites Kaplan et al. only as motivation for building a larger neural video codec. It scales individual codec modules by parameter count and reports BD-rate gains over a 21M baseline, but it fits no power law. It reports neither held-out loss against parameters, tokens or compute nor any extrapolation or allocation. So it does not test V1–V7, including V5, which concerns the power-law form in other modalities. Its scaling results are recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors find that enlarging the contextual encoder-decoder, contextual entropy model and temporal context mining module gives continuous gains. Slightly enlarging the motion modules helps, but enlarging them further degrades performance. CNNs beat mixed or Transformer architectures at similar size. The resulting NVC-1B (1.36B parameters) reaches -25.1% average BD-rate vs VTM on RGB, against -12.7% for the small baseline.
record.recipe_differences: The study scales components of a neural video codec and measures video compression, rather than fitting held-out language-model cross-entropy power laws or estimating compute-optimal language-model allocations.
record.method_sensitivity: Compression outcomes vary by coding module and architecture; the paper also notes a smaller gain on HEVC Class E and attributes it partly to using only 6 frames for multi-frame cascaded fine-tuning under GPU-memory limits.

fits_no_version.finding: In a neural video codec, gains from adding parameters depend on which module is enlarged. Motion encoder-decoder gains peak at 52M (15.4%) and drop to 1.5% at 96M. Contextual and temporal-context modules give sustained gains, up to 21.2% at 265M on Class D. At similar size, Transformer variants underperform CNNs or crash.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In neural video coding, compression gains from scaling parameters are module- and architecture-dependent and can be non-monotonic, with no single power-law trend reported.

record.problems: The results concern video compression rather than language-model held-out loss. The paper does not fit scaling curves or report uncertainty estimates. It reports unstable training and crashes for some configurations, and notes that limited GPU memory constrained fine-tuning to 6 frames.
record.rows_left_out: Other per-model and dataset outcomes appear in Figs. 2–6, but the text does not describe each separately; only outcomes explicitly stated in the prose are extracted here.

untested.parts: Entire version; no language-model loss or power-law fit.
Entire version; no fits extrapolated to larger runs.
Entire version. CNN vs Transformer codec architectures are compared at similar size, but the measure is video BD-rate, not language-model loss. Large differences were found there.
Video-codec scaling is studied, but no power-law form is fitted to loss or rate-distortion against parameters.
Entire version; no exponents or fitting choices.

record.verdict_notes: The supplied text is the arXiv v1 (TCSVT submission); the DOI points to TPAMI. The final NVC-1B vs baseline comparison (Tables III–IV) is not recorded as a row, but it bears on no version. No uncertainty or repeated runs are reported, and training crashes are frequent for larger motion modules.

rows.subject: M1
rows.operation_detail: Increased the motion encoder-decoder model size from the 21M-parameter baseline.
rows.measure: Video compression performance gain, reported as BD-rate reduction
rows.note: The paper reports this as the gain for M1 on HEVC Class C.

rows.subject: M3
rows.operation_detail: Further increased the motion encoder-decoder model size.
rows.measure: Video compression performance gain, reported as BD-rate reduction
rows.note: The paper says the gain drops when the motion encoder-decoder is increased further.

rows.subject: M4
rows.operation_detail: Scaled up the motion entropy model on top of M1.
rows.measure: Video compression performance gain, reported as BD-rate reduction
rows.baseline: Small baseline model; comparison described as M1's gain increasing from 15.4%
rows.note: The paper characterizes the additional gain from scaling this module as little.

rows.subject: M7
rows.operation_detail: Increased intermediate channels and added residual blocks in the contextual encoder-decoder.
rows.measure: Video compression performance gain, reported as BD-rate reduction
rows.note: The paper reports this as an example of improved compression performance.

rows.subject: M9
rows.operation_detail: Further increased the contextual encoder-decoder model size.
rows.measure: Video compression performance gain, reported as BD-rate reduction
rows.note: The paper reports sustained gains as this module is enlarged.

rows.subject: M12
rows.operation_detail: Scaled the contextual entropy model on top of the contextual encoder-decoder configurations.
rows.measure: Additional video compression performance gain, reported as BD-rate reduction
rows.note: The paper describes this added gain as an example of the benefit of a larger contextual entropy model.

rows.subject: M13
rows.operation_detail: Increased the temporal context mining module size relative to the small baseline.
rows.measure: Video compression performance gain, reported as BD-rate reduction
rows.note: The paper gives this as the gain at the 26M model size.

rows.subject: M15
rows.operation_detail: Further increased the temporal context mining module size.
rows.measure: Video compression performance gain, reported as BD-rate reduction
rows.note: The paper reports the gain increasing from 5.1% at 26M parameters.

rows.subject: M12
rows.operation_detail: Combined enlarged contextual encoder-decoder and contextual entropy model.

conditions.value: contextual encoder-decoder and contextual entropy model

rows.measure: Video compression performance gain, reported as BD-rate reduction
rows.note: This is the reference result for the temporal-context-module comparison.

rows.subject: M18
rows.operation_detail: Enlarged the temporal context mining module on top of the contextual encoder-decoder and entropy model.

conditions.value: temporal context mining with enlarged contextual modules

rows.measure: Video compression performance gain, reported as BD-rate reduction
rows.note: The paper reports this as an increase from the 14.2% gain for M12.

rows.subject: M12
rows.operation_detail: CNN architecture used as the comparison for the mixed CNN-Transformer model.
rows.measure: Video compression performance gain, reported as BD-rate reduction
rows.note: The paper compares this with M20, which has a similar but not identical parameter count.

rows.subject: M20
rows.operation_detail: Inserted SwinTransformer layers into the contextual entropy model on top of mixed-architecture M19.
rows.measure: Video compression performance gain, reported as BD-rate reduction
rows.note: The paper reports a smaller gain than the CNN-architecture M12 comparison.

rows.subject: M21
rows.operation_detail: Inserted a SwinTransformer layer after each residual block in the temporal context mining module.
rows.measure: Video compression performance gain, reported as BD-rate reduction
rows.note: The paper says adding Transformer layers to temporal context mining reduces the gain from M20's 9.4%.

rows.subject: M22
rows.operation_detail: Replaced the contextual encoder-decoder's convolutional layers and residual blocks with SwinTransformer layers.
rows.value: A little performance gain over the small baseline; much smaller gain than CNN counterpart M7
rows.note: No exact gain is stated in the text.
rows.check: The value is read as no exact number, but Fig. 6 appears to list M22 at about -1.1% / -6.0% BD-rate (Class C/D). The figure-text extraction is garbled, so verify against the figure.

rows.subject: M23
rows.operation_detail: Replaced contextual entropy-model convolutional layers and depth blocks with SwinTransformer layers.
rows.value: Model crash; PSNR loss of more than 4dB
rows.note: The crash makes BD-rate difficult to calculate, according to the paper.
rows.check: This is a training crash (PSNR loss >4dB) where BD-rate cannot be computed. It is not a measured reversal of a scaling effect, so 'reversed' overstates it.

rows.subject: M24
rows.operation_detail: Replaced temporal-context-module convolutional layers and residual blocks with SwinTransformer layers.
rows.value: Model crash; PSNR loss of more than 4dB
rows.note: The crash makes BD-rate difficult to calculate, according to the paper.
rows.check: Same as r15: a model crash with no BD-rate value, so 'reversed' is not readable as an effect direction.
